findings.summary: isPublished(article) dereferences article.draft without checking article is defined. articles.get(match[1]) returns undefined for any /blog/<slug> link whose slug isn't a real filename in packages/content/articles/ (a typo, a renamed/deleted post, or even an unrelated route like /blog/2 from pagination). That throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading draft)' inside the remark transform, which crashes the entire astro build rather than just failing to downgrade that one link. Reproduced directly: feeding stripLinksToDrafts a link to a nonexistent slug throws immediately. This is exactly the routine content-maintenance scenario (rename/delete a post, leave a stale backlink) the feature exists to make safe, so a bad/stale link taking down the whole build defeats the purpose.

findings.summary: Implementer's report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff touches exactly two files (astro.config.mjs and the new plugin) and adds zero test files. There is no test artifact in this change to verify that claim against, and no automated coverage exists for the link-stripping logic — including the crash case above, which a basic test (link to an unknown slug) would very plausibly have caught.

findings.summary: The plugin's isPublished only checks draft and date, omitting the import.meta.env.DEV bypass that the canonical isPublished in apps/web/src/utils/data-utils.ts uses. During `pnpm dev`, the rest of the site treats non-draft future-dated posts as published (DEV bypass), but this transform still strips inter-post links to them — a link-vs-page inconsistency visible only in local preview, not in production builds.
